macros.name: accidental
macros.doc: Using the \accidental command allows you to exclude accidentals from the published version should your publisher insist, while preserving the information about them in your source files should the publisher’s mind change.

macros.name: afterpoemskip
macros.doc: \afterpoemskip sets the vertical separation between the end of a poem and the title of the next poem.

macros.name: afterpoemtitleskip
macros.doc: \afterpoemtitleskip sets the vertical separation between a poem and its title.

macros.name: appendixincontentsfalse
macros.doc: If you wish to suppress contents entries for appendices, issue the boolean \appendixincontentsfalse.

macros.name: attribution
macros.doc: \epigraph, \headnote, \attribution, and \poemdedication set their arguments as epigraphs, headnotes, attributions, or dedications for poems or poetic sequences.

macros.name: backmattersectiontitle
macros.doc: Macros to set the titles of back matter sections such as textual notes.

macros.name: brokenline
macros.doc: \brokenline should be used where you wish to break the line without incrementing the line counter.

macros.name: centertitlesscheme
macros.doc: \centertitlesscheme will center the titles even if you do not center the verse block on the longest line.

macros.name: changecontentsheader
macros.doc: To change the running header on contents pages, issue \changecontentsheader{your header}.

macros.name: changecontentsname
macros.doc: To change the name of the Table of Contents (the default is CONTENTS) to Inhaltsverzeichnis, issue \changecontentsname{Inhaltsverzeichnis}.

macros.name: changeemendationsname
macros.doc: To change the name for the endnote section for emendations (the default is EMENDATIONS), issue \changeemendationsname{your version}.

macros.name: changeexplanationsheader
macros.doc: To change the running header (by default “Explanatory Notes to”) issue \changeexplanationsheader{your version}.

macros.name: changeexplanationsname
macros.doc: To change the name for the endnote section for explanatory notes (the default is EXPLANATORY NOTES), issue \changeexplanationsname{your version}.

macros.name: changenotesheader
macros.doc: To change the running header (by default “Textual Notes to”) issue \changenotesheader{your version}.

macros.name: changenotesname
macros.doc: To change the name for the endnote section for textual notes (the default is TEXTUAL NOTES), issue \changenotesname{your version}.

macros.name: changepoemindexheader
macros.doc: To change the running header (the default is “Index of Titles and First Lines”) issue \changepoemindexheader{your version}.

macros.name: changepoemindexname
macros.doc: To change the name for the index (the default is “Index of Titles and First Lines”, issue \changepoemindexname{your version}.

macros.name: changetextnotescontentsname
macros.doc: To change the name for the textual notes in the table of contents issue \changetextnotescontentsname{your version}.

macros.name: clearemptydoublepage
macros.doc: This macro is useful for making sure that the verso of a title page is blank.

macros.name: cleartorecto
macros.doc: A repeat of \cleardoublepage; clears to a recto (odd-numbered) page.

macros.name: contentsindentoneamount
macros.doc: You can change “contentsindentoneamount” (the amount a poem title is normally indented, by default 24pt) to, say, 36pt, by issuing \contentsindentoneamount=36pt in your preamble.

macros.name: contentsindenttwo
macros.doc: \contentsindentone, \contentsindenttwo, and so on are amounts to indent different hierarchical levels, say of poetic sequences and subsequences, in the table of contents.

macros.name: contentspoemtitlefont
macros.doc: \contentspoemtitlefont globally sets the font size (and leading) for poem titles in the table of contents.

macros.name: dateindent
macros.doc: You can move the placement of the date left or right by changing the value of the length \dateindent.

macros.name: definenewnotetype
macros.doc: If you define a new endnote type using \definenewnotetype, \definenewnotetype will also define a new \margref command to go with it.

macros.name: emendationsatfoot
macros.doc: To set your emendations as footnotes, issue \emendationsatfoot in your preamble.

macros.name: epigraph
macros.doc: \epigraph, \headnote, \attribution, and \poemdedication set their arguments as epigraphs, headnotes, attributions, or dedications for poems or poetic sequences.

macros.name: explanationsatfoot
macros.doc: To set your explanatory notes as footnotes, issue \explanationsatfoot.

macros.name: explanfootnotesparafalse
macros.doc: footnotes from \explanatory are set in “plain” mode (\explanfootnotesparafalse).

macros.name: explanfootnotesparatrue
macros.doc: To change explanatory footnotes from plain to para mode, for instance, issue \global\explanfootnotesparatrue.

macros.name: footnotesplitpoemtitle
macros.doc: \footnotesplitpoemtitle takes three arguments. The first argument is the first part of the title, up to the footnote mark, the second is the text of the footnote, and the third is the rest of the title.

macros.name: headnote
macros.doc: \epigraph, \headnote, \attribution, and \poemdedication set their arguments as epigraphs, headnotes, attributions, or dedications for poems or poetic sequences.

macros.name: headoffsetlength
macros.doc: Adjust \headoffsetlength to make the page numbers line up with the line numbers.

macros.name: hour
macros.doc: \hour is useful for typesetting the AM and the PM in the time.

macros.name: includeaccidentalsfalse
macros.doc: If you wish to exclude accidentals from your printed output, but to mark them in your source files, so that your published collation in the textual notes endnotes section consists only of substantives, issue \global\includeaccidentalsfalse in your preamble.

macros.name: includetypescriptsfalse
macros.doc: To exclude typescript variants, issue \global\includetypescriptsfalse in your preamble.

macros.name: indentedstanzaamount
macros.doc: The indentation will be of the length \indentedstanzaamount, which is by default set to \verseindentamount, which by default is 2 em.

macros.name: indexingonfalse
macros.doc: To turn indexing off, issue \global\indexingonfalse.

macros.name: JHdedication
macros.doc: the special commands \JHepigraph and \JHdedication, which place a mark in the margin showing where in the notes comments on that epigraph or dedication may be found.

macros.name: JHmarginparvshift
macros.doc: Vertical placement of the marginal mark for a textual note, relative to the baseline, is set by the length \JHmarginparvshift, which is set by default to 0 pt.

macros.name: JHmarksgutter
macros.doc: If you wish the marks to always be in the inner margin, issue \JHmarksgutter.

macros.name: JHshortdedication
macros.doc: \JHshortepigraph and \JHshortdedication, which set marginal marks pointing to where notes on the epigraph or dedication in the textual notes section may be found, in the manner of \JHpoemtitle.

macros.name: JHshortepigraph
macros.doc: \JHshortepigraph and \JHshortdedication, which set marginal marks pointing to where notes on the epigraph or dedication in the textual notes section may be found, in the manner of \JHpoemtitle.

macros.name: leftheader
macros.doc: \leftheader is for setting the left running header for the entire book (except for divider pages, the table of contents, the notes sections, and other special cases).

macros.name: longpage
macros.doc: \longpage and \shortpage are cumulative: issuing \longpage twice lengthens the page by two lines, and issuing \shortpage twice shortens the page by two lines.

macros.name: makeappendix
macros.doc: To make a an Appendix, or any other inserted prose section, use \makeappendix.

macros.name: makeemendations
macros.doc: To collect emendation notes, issue \makeemendations in your preamble.

macros.name: makeexplanatorynotes
macros.doc: To collect explanatory notes, issue \makeexplanatorynotes in your preamble.

macros.name: makepoemcontents
macros.doc: To make a table of contents for your poems, issue \makepoemcontents.

macros.name: makepoemcontents
macros.doc: To make a table of contents for your poems, issue \makepoemcontents.

macros.name: maketextnotes
macros.doc: To collect textual collations, issue \maketextnotes in your preamble.

macros.name: maketitlefootnoteslayered
macros.doc: If you are setting your textual notes or other notes at the foot of the page using “layers” of footnotes, you can treat these footnotes as just another layer by issuing the command \maketitlefootnoteslayered in your preamble.

macros.name: makeverselinenumbers
macros.doc: To turn on verse line numbering, issue \makeverselinenumbers.

macros.name: marginparsepmin
macros.doc: For centered verse, the distance between the line numbers and the verse can be set by setting the length of \marginparsepmin (not \marginparsep).

macros.name: marginsentencenumberformat
macros.doc: The format of marginal sentence numbers is set by \marginsentencenumberformat.

macros.name: marginsentencenumberstrue
macros.doc: To set sentence numbers in the margin, issue \marginsentencenumberstrue.

macros.name: missingpunct
macros.doc: To put the ∧ glyph into your text (used for recording places where a punctuation mark is missing in a variant), use \missingpunct.

macros.name: normalepigraphindentation
macros.doc: The margins for uncentered epigraphs and the like are controlled by the length \normalepigraphindentation (the default is 1.5em).

macros.name: noteindentation
macros.doc: You can change the amount of indentation by changing the value of the length \noteindentation (the default value is 1 em).

macros.name: paraend
macros.doc: You must mark the beginning and end of every paragraph in parallel prose passages with \parastart and \paraend.

macros.name: parastart
macros.doc: You must mark the beginning and end of every paragraph in parallel prose passages with \parastart and \paraend.

macros.name: pmclcontentsentry
macros.doc: There is a simple way of adding a new contents entry using the command \pmclcontentsentry.

macros.name: pmpara
macros.doc: \pmpara increments the paragraph counter, optionally puts the paragraph number in the running text, and optionally puts the paragraph number in the margin.

macros.name: pmparainmartrue
macros.doc: To set paragraph numbers in the margin, issue \pmparainmartrue.

macros.name: pmpararunningformat
macros.doc: The format of running paragraph numbers is set by \pmpararunningformat.

macros.name: pmpararunningtrue
macros.doc: To set paragraph numbers in the running text, issue \pmpararunningtrue.

macros.name: pmparmarformat
macros.doc: The format of marginal paragraph numbers is set by \pmparmarformat.

macros.name: pmsentence
macros.doc: \pmsentence increments the sentence counter, optionally puts the sentence number in the running text, and optionally puts the sentence number in the margin.

macros.name: poemdate
macros.doc: You can append the date of the poem with \poemdate.

macros.name: poemdedication
macros.doc: \epigraph, \headnote, \attribution, and \poemdedication set their arguments as epigraphs, headnotes, attributions, or dedications for poems or poetic sequences.

macros.name: poemfirstsectiontitle
macros.doc: \poemfirstsectiontitle is for the first section of a poem with many sections.

macros.name: poemlinelabel
macros.doc: \poemlinelabel enables crossreferences by line number.

macros.name: poemsectiontitle
macros.doc: \poemsectiontitle and \poemsubsectiontitle, as their names imply, set their arguments as the titles of sections or subsections of poems.

macros.name: poemsubsectiontitle
macros.doc: \poemsectiontitle and \poemsubsectiontitle, as their names imply, set their arguments as the titles of sections or subsections of poems.

macros.name: poemsubtitle
macros.doc: Subtitles of poems should be issued as the arguments to the \poemsubtitle command.

macros.name: poemtitle
macros.doc: \poemtitle, as its name implies, sets its argument as the title of the poem.

macros.name: poemtitlebaretitle
macros.doc: \poemtitlebaretitle, for instance simply sets the title in the text.

macros.name: poemtitlefont
macros.doc: \poemtitlefont globally sets the font size (and leading) for all poem titles in the main text.

macros.name: poemtitlenocontents
macros.doc: \poemtitlenocontents sends the title to the text and to the notes, but not to the contents.

macros.name: poemtitlenonotes
macros.doc: \poemtitlenonotes sends the title to the text and to the contents, but not to the notes.

macros.name: poemtitlenotitle
macros.doc: \poemtitlenotitle sends the title to the contents and the notes, but not to the main text.

macros.name: poemtitlepenalty
macros.doc: \poemtitlepenalty encourages but does not require a page break just before a poem title.

macros.name: prosesectiontitle
macros.doc: Prose sections may be titled with \prosesectiontitle which is essentially just \poemtitle, or \prosesectiontitlenotitle, which is essentially just \poemtitlenotitle.

macros.name: putexplanatory
macros.doc: \puttextnotes, and its siblings \putemendations and \putexplanatory, input the formatted endnotes sections into your document, and put entries for them into your table of contents.

macros.name: putmultiplepoemindex
macros.doc: To include the indices, and to add entries for them to the table of contents, issue \putmultiplepoemindex for each one.

macros.name: putpagenumberinnotesfalse
macros.doc: To turn off the appearance of the page number in the notes, issue \putpagenumberinnotesfalse.

macros.name: putpoemcontents
macros.doc: \putpoemcontents closes the file and reads it into your document.

macros.name: putpoemindex
macros.doc: \putpoemindex inputs the formatted index (after your raw entries have been processed by MakeIndex), and adds an entry for it into the table of contents.

macros.name: puttextnotes
macros.doc: \puttextnotes, and its siblings \putemendations and \putexplanatory, input the formatted endnotes sections into your document, and put entries for them into your table of contents.

macros.name: resetpagestyle
macros.doc: \resetpagestyle resets the page style to “main” (which is the same as the original “fancy”).

macros.name: rightheader
macros.doc: \volumeheader or \rightheader is for setting the right running header for that volume (except for divider pages, the table of contents, the notes sections, and other special cases).

macros.name: runningsentencenumberformat
macros.doc: \runningsentencenumberformat sets the format of running sentence numbers.

macros.name: runningsentencenumberstrue
macros.doc: \runningsentencenumberstrue sets sentence numbers in the running text.

macros.name: runoverindent
macros.doc: You can change the amount of indentation of runover lines with \runoverindent.

macros.name: sameword
macros.doc: To put the ∼ glyph in your note (used for recording places where the variant and the copy text have the same word, as for instance when recording a variation of punctuation) use \sameword.

macros.name: sentencelabel
macros.doc: To make labels that refer to sentences or paragraphs, issue \sentencelabel.

macros.name: sequencesectiontitle
macros.doc: \sequencetitle sets its argument as the title of the sequence, \sequencesectiontitle sets the titles of the sections of the sequence, and \sequencesubsectiontitle sets the titles of subsections of the sequence (there is even a command for the title of sub-subsections, \sequencesubsubsectiontitle).

macros.name: sequencesubsectiontitle
macros.doc: \sequencetitle sets its argument as the title of the sequence, \sequencesectiontitle sets the titles of the sections of the sequence, and \sequencesubsectiontitle sets the titles of subsections of the sequence (there is even a command for the title of sub-subsections, \sequencesubsubsectiontitle).

macros.name: sequencetitle
macros.doc: \sequencetitle sets its argument as the title of the sequence, \sequencesectiontitle sets the titles of the sections of the sequence, and \sequencesubsectiontitle sets the titles of subsections of the sequence (there is even a command for the title of sub-subsections, \sequencesubsubsectiontitle).

macros.name: setcontentsleaders
macros.doc: The argument to \setcontentsleaders can be whatever you wish to use to separate the title from the page number, such as a colon, a hard space (~), or even \hfil to flush the page number to the right margin.

macros.name: setpmmodulo
macros.doc: You can set the modulo for sentence marginal numbers by issuing \setpmmodulo.

macros.name: setverselinemodulo
macros.doc: \setverselinemodulo sets how often a marginal line number appears.

macros.name: sources
macros.doc: \sources sends information to the external file for textual notes, but does not tag what it sends with line numbers, hence its use for sending “sources.”

macros.name: stanzaatbottom
macros.doc: If you wish to change the symbol used to mark cases in which a break falls on a page turn, issue the command \stanzaatbottom, using as the argument whatever you wish to use to mark such cases.

macros.name: startverseline
macros.doc: You can have runover lines set their line number level with the beginning of the line by issuing \startverseline at the beginning of the line.

macros.name: startversopage
macros.doc: Verso pages should begin with \startversopage and end with \finishversopage.

macros.name: subappendixtitle
macros.doc: If you wish to add an Subappendix which you don’t want to start on a new page but do want to have a contents entry for, use \subappendixtitle instead of \makesubappendix.

macros.name: suppressfirstparatrue
macros.doc: To suppress the appearance of the first paragraph number, whether in the margin or in the running text, issue \suppressfirstparatrue.

macros.name: suppressfirstsentencetrue
macros.doc: To suppress the appearance of the first sentence number, whether in the margin or in the running text, issue \suppressfirstsentencetrue.

macros.name: testforauxonfirstrun
macros.doc: If you don’t want to listen to LaTeX complain about missing references during your first run, issue \testforauxonfirstrun, which won’t let \finish, \putexplanatory, \puttextnotes, or \putemendations run unless there is an .aux file for a previous run.

macros.name: textcenteringturnedonfalse
macros.doc: You can turn off centering of the verse block, without erasing all of the optional arguments, by issuing \textcenteringturnedonfalse.

macros.name: textcenteringturnedontrue
macros.doc: You can turn on centering the text block again by issuing \textcenteringturnedontrue.

macros.name: textnote
macros.doc: \textnote is used to capture variants and tie them to the correct line number.

macros.name: textnote
macros.doc: \textnote is used to capture variants and tie them to the correct line number.

macros.name: textnotesatfoot
macros.doc: To set your textual notes as footnotes, issue \textnotesatfoot in your preamble.

macros.name: tightleading
macros.doc: If you issue \tightleading you will redefine \normalsize and \small to use tighter leading.

macros.name: tweakbrokenline
macros.doc: Causes \brokenline to set the line number level with the beginning of the line if the number is on the left, level with the end of the line if the number is on the right.

macros.name: verseindent
macros.doc: The \verseindent command is to be used for formally indented lines.

macros.name: verseindent
macros.doc: The \verseindent command is to be used for formally indented lines.

macros.name: verseline
macros.doc: \verseline marks the end of every line as a prosodic unit (since a line of verse is not simply a carriage return), and advances the line counter.

macros.name: verselinenumbersfalse
macros.doc: To turn line numbering off, issue \global\verselinenumbersfalse.

macros.name: verselinenumbersgutter
macros.doc: If you want the line numbers to appear in the inner margins, issue \verselinenumbersgutter in your preamble.

macros.name: verselinenumbersouter
macros.doc: If you wish the line numbers to appear in the outer margins of each two-page spread, issue \verselinenumbersouter in your preamble.

macros.name: verselinenumberstoleft
macros.doc: To put all of the line numbers to the left, issue \verselinenumberstoleft in your preamble.

macros.name: verselinenumberstoright
macros.doc: \verselinenumberstoright puts the line numbers in the right margin.

macros.name: versemarginadjust
macros.doc: If you don’t want to center the verse block on the longest line, but do want to adjust its horizontal placement, you can adjust the placement of the verse block by changing the value of the length \versemarginadjust.

macros.name: versephantom
macros.doc: \brokenline is normally used with \versephantom, which adds white space exactly as long as its argument would have been had it been set in type.

macros.name: versewidth
macros.doc: The length \versewidth is used both to center the verse block and to place the title at the verse block’s left margin.

macros.name: volumeattribution
macros.doc: \volumeepigraph and \volumeattribution are for epigraphs and attributions on the divider pages.

macros.name: volumeepigraph
macros.doc: \volumeepigraph and \volumeattribution are for epigraphs and attributions on the divider pages.

macros.name: volumeheader
macros.doc: \volumeheader or \rightheader is for setting the right running header for that volume (except for divider pages, the table of contents, the notes sections, and other special cases).

macros.name: volumesectiontitle
macros.doc: \volumesectiontitle is for setting the title of a section of a volume. \volumesectiontitle merely prints the title in a large font in boldface in the text.

macros.name: volumesubtitle
macros.doc: \volumesubtitle is for setting the subtitle to a volume.

macros.name: volumetitle
macros.doc: \volumetitle is for the title of an individual volume within a Collected Poems.

macros.name: wholebooktitle
macros.doc: \wholebooktitle is for the title of the entire collection.

envs.name: indentedverse
envs.doc: To indent stanzas (or stretches of verse) relative to the margin you can use the indentedverse environment.

envs.name: indentedverse
envs.doc: To indent stanzas (or stretches of verse) relative to the margin you can use the indentedverse environment.

envs.name: maintitlepage
envs.doc: The maintitlepage environment is for the title page of the whole book.

envs.name: pmclverse
envs.doc: You can also use the special pmclverse environment, which enlarges the indentation of runover lines and the white space between stanzas.

envs.name: pmclverse
envs.doc: You can also use the special pmclverse environment, which enlarges the indentation of runover lines and the white space between stanzas.

envs.name: pmsection
envs.doc: You should put prose marked up for sentence and paragraph annotation in a pmsection environment.

envs.name: prosesectionnoreset
envs.doc: If for some reason you do not wish to reset the line number but continue on from where it left off at the end of the last prose section, use the prosesectionnoreset environment instead.

envs.name: volumetitlepage
envs.doc: The volumetitlepage environment is an environment for divider pages in collections made up of several volumes.
